title: Your SCM First-Week-Of-School Checklist
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents a twelve-item checklist designed to anchor the first week of school in classroom management fundamentals rather than allowing it to be crowded out by competing priorities. The items span greeting every student individually, teaching the classroom management plan in exacting detail with all gray area removed through explicit modeling, promising 100 percent follow-through, and thoroughly teaching and practicing core routines, transitions, the attention signal, and how to sit, listen, and ask a question. He rounds out the list with consistent pleasantness, calm enforcement of every broken rule, bringing humor into each day, and deliberately breathing and pausing rather than rushing. He is explicit that the checklist isn't a one-time task to complete and forget, but a standard of excellence that must be maintained through the entire year, and he addresses teachers already several weeks into the year directly, urging them to recommit to these fundamentals immediately rather than treating the first-week window as closed.
points: A twelve-item checklist anchors the first week of school in classroom management fundamentals: greeting, plan-teaching, routines, transitions, consistency, and calm enforcement.
All gray area in the classroom management plan should be removed through explicit modeling of what does and doesn't constitute breaking a rule.
Core routines, transitions, the attention signal, and how to sit/listen/ask a question should each be explicitly taught, modeled, and practiced.
The checklist is framed as an ongoing standard to maintain all year, not a one-time task to complete in week one.
Teachers already several weeks into the year are urged to recommit to these fundamentals immediately rather than treating the first-week window as closed.
quotes: You no doubt have a packed schedule the first week of school, but classroom management must take precedence.
Because it’s the foundation upon which effective teaching is built. It also ensures your peace and protects your students’ right to learn and enjoy school.
Remove all gray area by modeling what does and doesn’t constitute breaking your rules.
The first week is only a start. Check the twelve items off if you wish, but their excellence must remain your priority until the last minute of the last day of school.
And if you’ve already started school, and are in your third week, for example, go back and recommit to them now.
Are you going to be the one person they need right now more than ever or yet another mediocre teacher that will only set them even farther behind?
